# candidate's ENCLOSING FUNCTION and searches them for the bound
# mutable-state token.  It ALSO consults the host control TU, because
# a decision can reach the mutable host state through a callee that
# lives OUTSIDE the parser census set.

# depend on mutable host state.  The tool's exit is the honest
# signal, and the per-candidate verdicts are the evidence.

Declares jmp_buf stmt_recovery; SAVES cc->current_recovery into outer_recovery; OVERWRITES cc->current_recovery with &stmt_recovery; calls setjmp(stmt_recovery).  It OWNS setjmp and WRITES the recovery state.

Reads and writes the host AST body list (listAppend(body->stms,stmt)); restores cc->current_recovery = outer_recovery; drives the token cursor.  REQUIRES nonlocal recovery and performs host graph writes.
The WHOLE-FUNCTION parseStatement.  Owns the recovery checkpoint interaction, drives the token cursor, constructs every Ast node and calls the statement constructor callbacks.
The WHOLE-FUNCTION parseExpr.  A recursive descent loop over the token cursor that builds the expression AST and owns the recovery state.

column1: # The eighteen candidates with NO mutable-host-state dependence are
# CAND-018, CAND-021, CAND-022, CAND-023, CAND-025, CAND-026,
# NO_MUTABLE_HOST_STATE_DEPENDENCE DOES NOT MEAN BOUNDED.  Three of
# those eighteen are excluded on a DIFFERENT ground: CAND-038,
# CAND-039 and CAND-040 have an unbounded HOST STRING input and/or a
# NEW HOST STRING output.  "The decision reads no mutable symbol
# table" is NOT the same claim as "the decision has a bounded
# projection", and the registry keeps them separate.
# SUB-005's dependence is the ONLY one that is TRANSITIVE through a
# callee OUTSIDE the census set, and it is therefore the one that a
# "read the visible signature" judgement would most easily miss: the
# decision's own signature takes only a Lexeme pointer and a length.
